title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

reading.body:
This is insider misuse of a deployed system, not a failure of the system's accuracy. A license plate reader network built to support police investigations was queried by the person who controlled access to it, for a purpose unrelated to any investigation. The failure sits at the query layer, where a legitimate credential was used to run searches against people the operator knew personally.

Catching this kind of use requires someone other than the operator to look at what was queried and why. That means retaining query records, tying searches to a stated investigative purpose, and reviewing them independently. The facts given do not say whether any of that existed in Sedgwick or whether anyone reviewed the searches while they were happening.

The reported counts do not agree: the headline says 164 uses and the summary says 228. The account rests on a single outlet's reporting of a Kansas certification order, and the order is a finding by a state body rather than a criminal conviction.

reports.title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

summary: From June to October 2023, Sedgwick, Kansas, Police Chief Lee Nygaard reportedly used Flock Safety license plate readers 228 times to check where his ex-girlfriend and her new boyfriend were, according to a Kansas certification order. The order said he also followed them in a police vehicle and admitted jealousy influenced his conduct. Nygaard resigned in October 2023 and later lost his police certification.
title_en: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend
